title: Algebra: Sequences, Series, Matrices & Complex Numbers
confusion: ❌ 'Sequence and series are the same thing.' ✅ Sequence = ordered list of terms; Series = SUM of those terms.
❌ 'S∞ = a/(1−r) works for any GP.' ✅ Only valid when |r| < 1. If |r| ≥ 1, the sum diverges.
❌ 'Every square matrix has an inverse.' ✅ Only if determinant ≠ 0. Singular matrices (det = 0) have no inverse.
❌ 'i² = −1 means i is a real number.' ✅ i is imaginary. Complex numbers extend reals: z = a + ib.
notes: **Geometric progression (GP):** aₙ = arⁿ⁻¹; Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1); S∞ = a/(1 − r) for |r| < 1. AM ≥ GM.

**Matrices:** order m × n, addition, scalar multiplication, matrix multiplication (row × column). Determinant of 2×2 and 3×3; singular if det = 0; inverse A⁻¹ = adj(A)/|A| for solving simultaneous equations (Cramer's rule).
**Complex numbers:** i² = −1; z = x + iy with modulus |z| = √(x² + y²) and conjugate z̄. Multiplication/division in polar form uses r(cos θ + i sin θ).
